title: The Late Garden
premise: Lior Fairweather, a single parent and owner of the town's only bookshop, has spent fifteen years keeping life small and safe after a devastating betrayal. When their estranged family demands a plus-one for the annual reunion at the Almeida vineyard, Lior persuades Wren Halloway—the town's ambitious, guarded mayor—to pose as their partner. The fake date turns real by dessert, but Wren is secretly negotiating to sell the vineyard to a developer whose money would secure her political future, threatening both Lior's shop and the town's memory. As first harvest approaches, Lior must choose between protecting their heart and fighting for what they love, while Wren must decide whether power is worth the corruption it demands. They end up together, but only after Wren publicly kills the deal, loses her career, and plants something new in the late garden.
about_author: Tamsin Almeida is the pen name of a former bookseller who spent a decade shelving other people's love stories before writing her own. She lives near a working vineyard and insists the best romances ripen slowly, like late-season fruit.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet Lior closing the bookshop, navigating school pickup for their daughter Juniper, and dodging a letter from the Fairweather family demanding attendance at the reunion. A chance collision with Mayor Wren Halloway at the post office crackles with mutual irritation and reluctant attraction. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: The Proposal
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cornered by their sister's phone call, Lior impulsively asks Wren—whom they barely know—to be their fake date to the reunion at the Almeida vineyard. Wren, needing to charm rural voters before an election, agrees with a handshake contract of rules. Emotional beat: reckless hope dressed up as practicality.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The family reunion: sharp-tongued relatives, old wounds about Lior's past betrayal, and Wren performing devotion so convincingly that the line blurs. By dessert they're holding hands under the table for real. On the drive home, almost-kiss number one. Emotional beat: the fake thing becoming terrifyingly true.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren drafts new 'rules' to keep distance, but keeps breaking them—lunches at the bookshop, walks that last too long. Meanwhile she meets privately with developer Marcus Vane about selling the vineyard land, telling herself it's just due diligence. Emotional beat: self-deception compounding; power beginning to taste sweet.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior and Juniper visit the vineyard's heritage garden, where Lior's late grandmother once worked, and discover Vane's survey stakes marking the old rows. Wren lies smoothly when asked. Lior finds a hidden letter hinting Wren knew about the sale all along. Emotional beat: first crack of doubt beneath new love.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night before first harvest: a town festival where Wren gives a rousing speech about preserving local heritage—while the Vane contract sits unsigned in her bag. She and Lior finally kiss, fully, honestly. Then Lior sees Vane's name on Wren's phone screen. Emotional beat: joy at its peak, one hour before the fall.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Letter
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Confrontation at the bookshop: Lior lays out the evidence, and Wren's justifications—funding the school, saving her career—sound exactly like the person who betrayed Lior fifteen years ago. Wren leaves rather than choose. Juniper, heartbreakingly perceptive, asks if the mayor was ever real. Emotional beat: history repeating; the whole heart withdrawn.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Signing day. Alone in her office with the pen uncapped, Wren reads her grandmother's old campaign letters and realizes she has become everything she ran against. She tears up the contract, resigns her candidacy, and walks into the harvest festival crowd to find Lior. Emotional beat: power refused; the cost counted and paid willingly.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Public reckoning: Wren confesses everything at the festival, losing face and future, then asks Lior for nothing—not forgiveness, not a date, just the truth. Lior, who has lent pieces of their heart for fifteen years, decides to risk the whole thing. They pick grapes together as dawn breaks over the vines. Emotional beat: vulnerability chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: The Late Garden
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue-style. Months later: the vineyard saved by a community trust, the bookshop thriving, Wren planting the restored heritage garden with dirt under her nails and no title at all. Juniper calls her by her first name. In the late garden, among things planted too late but growing anyway, Lior proposes nothing grander than next season—and forever. Emotional beat: love rooted where memory and courage meet.
